description: STRENGTHENING VERMONT PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE AND DATA SYSTEMS - SIX MONTHS INTO THE  COVID-19 PANDEMIC RESPONSE, VERMONT DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH STAFF WERE COMPLETELY MOBILIZED, EXCEPT FOR ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS THAT COULD NOT BE INTERRUPTED. AT THE PEAK OF THE RESPONSE, OVER 80% OF ALL WORK HOURS REPORTED BY STAFF WERE FOR PANDEMIC RESPONSE. THE DEPARTMENT’S FIRST PRIORITY WAS STAFF AUGMENTATION TO PROVIDE RELIEF TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH WORKFORCE. BETWEEN AUGUST 2020 AND APRIL 2022, THE DEPARTMENT SECURED APPROVAL FOR 117 NEW POSITIONS, FUNDED BY CDC COVID-19 SUPPLEMENTS. THIS IS AN OVERALL INCREASE OF 21% TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH WORKFORCE, WITH ABOUT ONE-THIRD OF THE NEW POSITIONS ASSIGNED TO DISTRICT OFFICES. BY LATE FALL 2021, MANY OF THESE NEW POSITIONS WERE FILLED AND DEPLOYED TO THE PANDEMIC RESPONSE, PRIMARILY FOCUSED IN THE CRITICAL AREAS OF EPIDEMIOLOGY, LABORATORY SCIENCES, IMMUNIZATION, AND HEALTH EQUITY. THE FUNDS TO SUPPORT THESE POSITIONS ARE GENERALLY SHORT-TERM (<5 YEARS) IN NATURE WITH NO EXPRESSED COMMITMENT OF CONTINUED FUNDING. HOWEVER, THE NEED FOR THE WORK OF THESE POSITIONS IS LONG-TERM AND ONGOING. WITHOUT IT, WE WILL BE REQUIRED TO SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE OUR WORKFORCE, ESSENTIALLY ELIMINATING ANY GAINS AND POTENTIAL FOR FUTURE PROGRESS, PARTICULARLY WITH RESPECT TO THOSE DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTED BY THE PANDEMIC.  ALTHOUGH THE WORKFORCE GAINS NOTED ABOVE STRENGTHENED OUR CAPACITY IN ADDRESSING SOME OF THE TEN ESSENTIAL PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES, THERE ARE COMPONENTS WITHIN EACH THAT ARE LACKING INCLUDING DATA COLLECTION, ANALYSIS, REPORTING, QUALITY AND MODERNIZATION. MANY OF OUR DATA SYSTEMS ARE ANTIQUATED AND IN NEED OF UPGRADING TO BECOME FULLY INTEROPERABLE, ALLOWING US TO MOVE FROM MANUAL PROCESSES TO AUTOMATED ONES, THEREBY IMPROVING OUR RESPONSE TO EMERGING EVENTS. OUR LABORATORY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND INFECTIOUS DISEASE DATA SYSTEM (NBS), FOR EXAMPLE, ARE OVERDUE WITH REGARDS TO UPDATING AND INTEROPERABILITY, AND OTHERS SUCH AS OUR VITAL RECORDS AND IMMUNIZATION SYSTEMS ARE ANTIQUATED. SOME FALL INTO BOTH CATEGORIES – BEHIND SCHEDULE WITH RESPECT TO MODERN CAPABILITIES AS WELL AS BEING VERY OLD. BECAUSE OF A LACK OF RESOURCES AND CAPACITY, WE HAVE HAD TO INSTITUTE WORKAROUNDS TO MEET THE INCREASING DEMANDS FOR DATA AND DATA SHARING. THE STRESS OF THE COVID-19 RESPONSE HIGHLIGHTED THE WEAKNESSES OF SUCH MAKESHIFT SOLUTIONS AS THEY ARE PRONE TO FAILURE, REQUIRE SIGNIFICANT MANUAL WORK, AND DON’T TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE. DATA EXCHANGE AND INTEGRATION WITH THE VERMONT HEALTH INFORMATION EXCHANGE IS ALSO A PRIORITY AND SIMPLY CANNOT OCCUR WITHOUT INVESTMENTS IN THESE AREAS.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The purpose of the Emerging Infections Programs (EIP) is to assist in local, state, and national efforts to prevent, control, and monitor the public health impact of infectious diseases. The EIP cooperative agreement was formed in 1995 as a key component of CDC’s national strategy to address and reduce emerging infectious disease (EID) threats.  The EIP is a population-based network of state health agencies and their collaborators, including (but not limited to) academic institutions, local health departments, public health and clinical laboratories, infection control professionals, and healthcare providers.   The unique strength of the EIP lies in the network’s ability to quickly translate surveillance and research activities into informed policy and public health practice.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The intent of this program is to fund state, local, and territorial public health departments for HHS Secretarial declared and non-declared public health emergencies having an overwhelming impact on jurisdictional resources. These emergencies require federal support to effectively respond to, manage, and address a significant public health threat. CDC seeks to enhance the Nation’s ability to rapidly mobilize and respond to specific public health crises or emergencies. In addition to immediate response activities, this program provides a mechanism to accelerate readiness for an impending infectious disease threat or other public health crises identified on the event horizon.
cfda_info.cfda_title: Public Health Emergency Response:  Cooperative Agreement for Emergency Response: Public Health Crisis Response
